vectors.text: I'm Ajaykumar Balakannan. Most people just call me Ajay. I'm a data scientist based in Dallas. I finished my Master's in Data Science at the University of Maryland in May 2026, graduating with a 3.74/4.0. I've built production ML, NLP, and LLM systems on big operational datasets. Anomaly detection on 15M+ job market records, a no-show prediction model that reroutes counseling appointments, salary models across 40,000+ US zip codes. What I like is owning the whole path, from the ingestion pipeline to the model to the dashboard someone actually opens on Monday morning. I'm looking for full-time data science, ML engineering, and analytics roles.

vectors.source: portfolio (self-description, grounded in the work below)
vectors.text: How I work. I build end to end instead of handing off a notebook. At Maryland that meant I wrote the DuckDB pipeline, trained the model, and built the Tableau dashboard the counseling staff actually use. All of it, because a model nobody can act on isn't really finished. I care most about whether the thing gets used. The numbers I'm proudest of are adoption numbers, not leaderboard scores. At UMD that was 25% better resource utilization from the no-show model. At Canaria it was the LLM reporting workflows saving about 15 analyst hours a week. Different jobs, different numbers. I use explainability by default. I put SHAP on the no-show model so the counseling team could see why someone got flagged, otherwise they'd have no reason to trust it. I'm also pretty suspicious of my own data. I ran PyOD and Cleanlab validation across Canaria's 15M+ records specifically to find what the pipeline was quietly getting wrong. And I'd rather measure something than argue about it. For TravelGenie I load tested EC2 against ECS Fargate at 50 to 100 concurrent users instead of guessing which one was cheaper. Generally I'd rather ship something small that works than something clever that only demos well.

My timeline, so the dates line up. Aug 2020 to May 2024: B.Tech in Electrical and Electronics Engineering at Sri Krishna College of Engineering and Technology, Coimbatore, India. Mar 2023 to Jul 2024: Data and Analytics Engineer at AastraZen Technologies in Chennai, which overlapped my final year of the B.Tech and continued a couple of months past graduation. Sep 2024 to now: Data Scientist at the University of Maryland Counseling Center in College Park. May 2025 to Aug 2025, so the summer of 2025: Data Science Intern at Canaria Inc. in New York, which is the most recent full-time summer role I've held. May 2026: I graduated from Maryland with my Master's in Data Science. I'm still at the UMD Counseling Center, living in Dallas, and looking for full-time roles.

I did my Master's in Data Science at the University of Maryland, College Park, and graduated in May 2026 with a GPA of 3.74/4.0 (an older internal document says 3.78 from an earlier term). The coursework that mattered most was Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, Big Data Systems, and Deep Learning. Maryland is a big public R1 school just outside Washington DC. A few of my NLP and deep learning course projects came out of that program, including the RNN comparison, the n-gram modeling work, and the gun violence coverage analysis.

vectors.text: My undergrad is a B.Tech in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from Sri Krishna College of Engineering and Technology (SKCET) in Coimbatore, India, Aug 2020 to May 2024, CGPA 8.4/10.0. SKCET is an autonomous private engineering college founded in 1998 and affiliated with Anna University, with NBA accredited programs and a spot in the NIRF engineering top 100. Coursework included Microcontrollers, Power System Analysis, Python, and Machine Learning in Energy Systems. I think coming from electrical engineering rather than CS is part of why I like systems that touch the physical world. The farmland detection project was hardware and vision together, not just a model in a notebook.

Since Sep 2024 I've been a Data Scientist at the University of Maryland Counseling Center in College Park, working there alongside my Master's. The Counseling Center is the university's mental health service for students, so everything I build touches appointment access and staff time. I built a no-show prediction model on student appointment records, Random Forest plus LightGBM with SHAP for explainability. It triggers automated outreach and lifted resource utilization by 25%. I used Sentence-Transformers (SetFit) and BERTopic to classify 4,000+ pieces of student feedback from e-forms and audio transcripts, which surfaced sentiment and service themes the counseling staff now act on. I engineered Python, DuckDB, and SQL pipelines that pull 12+ years of operational records into version controlled data models, and that's the backbone under both the models and the KPI reporting. I automated the data refresh behind our Tableau and Power BI dashboards covering utilization, cancellations, and peak demand, which cut manual reporting turnaround by 60%. I also ran hypothesis testing and sentiment analysis on 10+ years of student survey data. That helped administrators get budget increases two quarters running, and fed into resource allocation discussions that cut redundant resources by 20%.

I was a Data Science Intern at Canaria Inc. in New York from May 2025 to Aug 2025, so the summer of 2025. I built v0 statistical models and then v1 PyCaret pipelines (Isolation Forest, KNN, HBOS, COPOD, OCSVM) over 15M+ job market records, containerized with Docker. That cut false positive anomaly flags by 35% in production. I built a salary prediction model with LightGBM, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting across 40,000+ US zip codes, segmented by SOC code, location, and seniority. It ran inside an MLflow tracked, auto-recalibrating ClickHouse pipeline for real-time forecasting, deployed on AWS, and it helped bring in 10+ new clients. I ran PyOD and Cleanlab validation over those same 15M+ distributed records to catch statistical outliers. I designed Polars and PySpark ingestion pipelines across three cloud systems (ClickHouse, PostgreSQL, and AWS S3) to keep the job market data clean for everything downstream. And I built LLM workflows over unstructured text that automated summarization and reporting, which saved about 15 analyst hours a week.

A bit about Canaria Inc., where I interned in summer 2025. Canaria is a New York based job market data startup, founded in 2022. They sell research grade labor market intelligence: roughly a billion deduplicated job postings enriched with 100+ fields, SOC occupation codes, salary signals, and a taxonomy of 40,000+ skills, plus company profiles and AI extracted compensation data. Their customers are in HR, recruitment, workforce analytics, and financial modeling. That context explains the shape of my work there. When your product is the dataset itself, a bad posting or a mis-scored salary is a defect that ships straight to clients. So most of my summer was anomaly detection, validation, and recalibration rather than modeling for its own sake.

From Mar 2023 to Jul 2024 I was a Data and Analytics Engineer at AastraZen Technologies in Chennai. It overlapped my final year of undergrad and ran a couple of months past graduation. I fine-tuned a Hugging Face DistilBERT model for automated support ticket categorization and built semantic search on a vector database, which cut manual ticket triage time by 45% across client support workflows. I migrated a legacy client database to a hybrid MongoDB and PostgreSQL setup with dbt managed transformation layers, improving query throughput by 40% and making real-time reporting possible for a mid-market client. I also built a real-time streaming pipeline on Apache Kafka feeding a central AWS S3 data lake, supporting concurrent analytics across 5+ client accounts at 99.5% uptime. This is the job where I learned data engineering properly. Most of what I know about keeping pipelines alive in production came from here.

A bit about AastraZen Technologies, where I worked from Mar 2023 to Jul 2024. It's a private software services company, incorporated in March 2019, based in Sholinganallur, Chennai. They do software development services and IT corporate training, and they sell SaaS customer engagement tooling that support, sales, and marketing teams use to talk to their customers. Because it's a services company spread across several client accounts rather than one product team, I ended up touching a lot of different stacks. Support ticket NLP for one client, a database migration for another, Kafka streaming shared across several. That's how I got breadth pretty early.

My technical stack. AI and machine learning: LLM orchestration (Claude, MCP), generative AI, LightGBM, XGBoost, SHAP, Isolation Forest, ARIMA, SetFit, BERTopic, DistilBERT, scikit-learn, PyCaret, HBOS, COPOD, OCSVM, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, SVM. Data platforms and warehousing: Snowflake, ClickHouse, PostgreSQL, Databricks, Redshift, MongoDB, DuckDB, AWS (S3, EC2), MLflow, dbt, Kafka. Languages and processing: Python, SQL, R, Pandas, NumPy, Polars, PySpark, PyOD, Cleanlab, MATLAB. Visualization and reporting: Tableau, Power BI, Qlik Sense, Sigma, Quarto and Jupyter, KPI tracking, root cause analysis. Data engineering and cloud: Docker, Apache Spark, Hadoop, Azure, Git and CI/CD, relational data modeling. Short version: Python and SQL are the daily drivers, LightGBM is my default first model on tabular problems, and I'm happy owning the AWS and pipeline side instead of treating it as someone else's job.

I hold the AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate certification (SAA-C03) from Amazon Web Services Training and Certification. You can verify it at https://www.credly.com/badges/a27d9d8a-3fbb-45ec-a576-86c943074d35. I went for it because I was already deploying on AWS at Canaria and wanted to learn the architecture side properly instead of picking it up piecemeal.

I'm a Microsoft Certified Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300). The credential page is https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/users/ajaykumarbalakannan-2262/credentials/bdc6daa31e1d313b. Power BI is one of the two BI tools I use in production at the UMD Counseling Center, the other being Tableau.

Other certifications and training I've done, mostly earlier in my education. Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate on Coursera, 8 courses covering spreadsheets, SQL, Tableau, R, and the full data analysis lifecycle, completed Feb 17 2025, verifiable at coursera.org/verify/professional-cert/KD5MOZ1GQKG4. Celonis Academy Process Automation Bootcamp (Foundational), issued 07-09-2022, verifiable at credly.com/go/KN5UxdSW. MathWorks Machine Learning Onramp, 100% completion, 07 September 2022. Automation Anywhere University, Building Scalable Bots Using Automation 360 (RPA), completed 10/08/2021. And a Udemy Python for Beginners course by Bharath Thippireddy, 13.5 hours, completed Aug 18 2022. The two that actually carry professional weight are the AWS Solutions Architect and the Microsoft PL-300.

TravelGenie is my AI travel planning system, built Dec 2025. It's at github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/TravelGenie. It plans a trip by pulling flights, hotels, events, weather, currency, and traffic through one request instead of ten browser tabs. The architecture is seven standalone MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, Flight, Hotel, Event, Geocoder, Weather, Finance, and Traffic and Crowd, each doing exactly one job, with Claude orchestrating and chaining their outputs. So it geocodes a location, then searches flights and hotels near it, then checks the weather for those dates. Flight, hotel, and event data comes from SerpAPI. Open-Meteo and OpenStreetMap need no API key. It ships as a Streamlit web UI and a Slack bot, and the MCP servers can run directly inside Claude Desktop too. It deploys via Docker or AWS using ECS Fargate, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager, and CloudWatch, provisioned with CloudFormation. The part I'd point at is the benchmarking. I load tested EC2 against ECS Fargate under sustained and stress load at 50 to 100 concurrent users, and Fargate matched EC2's 460 requests per second on roughly half the compute. MIT licensed.

vectors.text: Farmland wildlife intrusion detection, Mar 2023, at github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Framland_Protection. It's a non-lethal alternative to electric fencing and chemical repellents for keeping wildlife off farmland. A camera watches the field continuously. YOLOv3 does real-time animal detection at around 90% accuracy, with non-maximum suppression to drop redundant boxes. Then a second validation stage, a CNN for species verification plus a Random Forest to filter false positives, cuts false alarms by about 40%. A confirmed detection triggers an Arduino controller that fires a deterrent matched to the animal: sound for nocturnal animals, light for herbivores like deer, water sprinklers for medium sized ones. Every detection gets logged with image, species, time, and location, which is useful for conservation and census work. One honest correction. The README's future work section mentions upgrading to YOLOv5, and YOLOv3 is what I actually implemented and demoed, even though a couple of later materials (a portfolio tag, one resume version) say YOLOv5. It won 2nd place out of 500+ teams and a $300 prize at the National Technocraft Hackathon (Technocraft Booth Project Competition 2022-23, held at COEP in Pune on 2nd May 2023), and the work was published in BIOGECKO, Vol 12 Issue 03, 2023. We built and tested a hardware prototype alongside the software.

Bitcoin price forecasting, 2025, a Qlik Sense project under causify-ai/tutorials (TutorTask146). End to end it does live BTC price collection, ARIMA and XGBoost forecasting at around 85% predictive accuracy, automated ingestion, validation and transformation workflows, and interactive Qlik Sense dashboards for real-time visibility into volatility and market drivers. It cut manual reporting effort by about 40%.

vectors.text: The Sage Ventures multifamily real estate analytics pipeline, 2025, at github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/RealEstateModelling. Being straight about this one: it's a self-built portfolio project, not client work. I simulated the data infrastructure, reporting, and BI of a multifamily real estate portfolio to show SQL, Python, Power BI, and Excel skills for a junior data analyst type role, and the underlying data is synthetic, generated with Faker. Sage Ventures is a real firm though, a Baltimore and Pikesville, Maryland real estate company founded in 2004 that acquires, develops, rehabilitates, and manages multifamily properties around the DC and Baltimore region. That's what I modeled the scenario on. The pipeline runs in one command (run_pipeline.py) across five phases. generate_data.py builds a SQLite DB and raw CSVs, feature_engineering.py creates 15+ engineered features, adhoc_analysis.py produces 5 business reports, excel_report.py builds a 7 sheet workbook, and visualize.py generates 10 charts. The data model goes properties to units to tenants to rent_roll, plus properties to maintenance and properties to occupancy_monthly. Stack is Python, SQLite, SQL, Pandas, openpyxl, Matplotlib, and Power BI. Some illustrative findings from the simulated portfolio: 67% average occupancy against a 93% target, $2.14M annual loss to lease, $19,864 in delinquency exposure, and 533 open maintenance tickets past SLA.

The CANARIA Anomaly Detection System at github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Version-1-anomaly is the job market anomaly detection work tied to my Canaria internship. It finds unusual patterns in job posting data at three levels: US level (geo_level by source), state level (state by source), and SOC occupation level (SOC code by source). Parquet files get read in configurable batches, 50,000 rows by default, cleaned and validated, then stored in MongoDB under a rolling window (45 days by default) so the models keep adapting to recent data without storage growing forever. Feature engineering generates 18 features per record: rolling statistics over 7, 14, and 28 days, temporal features like day of week and month, statistical measures like z-scores and MAD, and expanding window long-term patterns. The model layer is a 7 model ensemble, PyCaret's Isolation Forest, KNN, and SVM plus PyOD's HBOS, COPOD, OCSVM, and CBLOF. Scores get averaged for robustness and compared against per-segment quantile thresholds, with cooldown logic so it doesn't spam alerts. Output is CSV results with scores, plus logging and performance monitoring.

Resume Optimiser and Outreach Automation at github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Resume_Optimiser is two tools in one repo, built in 2026. First, a resume optimizer CLI (resume_api.py). You paste in a job description and get back a tailored one page LaTeX resume, a cover letter paragraph, and an email draft, generated through the Claude API and compiled with pdflatex. Second, an outreach web app in Next.js. You upload a contacts CSV, attach a resume, write one email template, preview every personalized message, and send the batch through Gmail via OAuth. It integrates with Apollo.io to find and reveal contacts at a target company across leadership and role matched tiers, and writes a custom paragraph per contact using Claude Haiku plus a free web search cascade (Tavily, Exa, Brave) to get real context on each person. There are guardrails that reject generic AI sounding phrasing or a too casual tone and retry with a correction. Cost and usage get tracked per call, tokens, cache hits, and USD, and surfaced in an analytics view, because I wanted to actually know what the thing costs to run.

BudgetPlay at github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/BudgetPlay is a participatory budgeting simulator I built for an Anthropic Hackathon, Track 3, Governance and Accessibility. You explore how a city sized budget is allocated, move sliders to rebalance spending across categories, read a Claude generated plain language narrative explaining the tradeoffs of your reallocation, and optionally submit your budget as a vote grouped by region. A companion Government Pulse dashboard aggregates submissions so community averages can be compared against the official budget, with percentage point shifts by category and short recommendation blurbs. Stack is Node.js and Express on the backend, a static frontend with Tailwind, Chart.js, and vanilla JS, and the Anthropic Messages API for the narrative endpoint. The budget data is sample and educational, not a real government budget.

A comparative analysis of RNN architectures for sentiment classification, from my UMD coursework, at github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Sentiment-Analysis. I implemented and compared plain RNN, LSTM, and Bidirectional LSTM on the IMDb movie review dataset, varying activation functions (sigmoid, ReLU, tanh), optimizers (Adam, SGD, RMSprop), sequence lengths of 25, 50, and 100 words, and gradient clipping on and off, to see how each choice moves classification performance.

N-gram language modeling and evaluation, UMD coursework, at github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/N_Gram_Modelling. I implemented and evaluated Maximum Likelihood Estimation n-gram language models from unigram through 4-gram on the Penn Treebank dataset, looking at the tradeoff between n-gram order and the role of smoothing and backoff in handling data sparsity, with perplexity evaluation and text generation.

A comparative analysis of gun violence coverage across news outlets, from my UMD NLP coursework, at github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Comparative_Analysis_HW5. I used NLP techniques including coreference resolution with spaCy to analyze how CNN, Fox News, The New York Times, and The Wall Street Journal portray victims and shooters across gun violence incidents, over a dataset of 100 articles, 25 per outlet.

My team took 2nd place out of 500+ teams and a $300 prize at the National Technocraft Hackathon (Technocraft Booth Project Competition 2022-23, hosted by the Alumni Association of the College of Engineering Pune and the COEP Charitable Foundation USA, held 2nd May 2023) for the farmland wildlife intrusion detection project. It was a team project during my B.Tech at Sri Krishna College. The findings were later published in BIOGECKO, Vol 12 Issue 03, 2023, a New Zealand biology journal, on YOLO based AI detection with automated deterrents.

Two earlier things from my undergrad years. I went to PRAYATNA, a 2 day hands-on workshop run by Microsoft and Walmart at IIT Chennai in May 2022, on web and app development with HTML/CSS, JavaScript, and responsive design. And I did a web development internship and industrial project at Denshi Solutions in Erode, India, from 04/04/2023 to 05/06/2023, as part of a 9 student team from Sri Krishna College's final year Electrical and Electronics Engineering program, working on product development and the web build out.
